title: Valles Marineris
subtitle: The grandest canyon
yt_title: The Grand Canyon of Mars 🏜️ | Ep. 97 #shorts
description:
Episode 97 of a daily journey through the universe. 🏜️
We explore Valles Marineris on Mars: about 4,000 km long, up to 7 km deep and 200 km wide, ten times longer than the Grand Canyon, discovered by Mariner 9 in 1971–72, and formed when the crust cracked open, not by a river.

➡️ Tomorrow, Episode 98: Next stop, Phobos. A moon that is falling into Mars.
Start from Episode 1 "Leaving Earth" on the channel.
Follow so you don't miss a stop. A new episode every day.

segments.text: Episode ninety-seven. Next stop... Valles Marineris.
Next to the giant volcanoes of Mars lies the biggest canyon system in the solar system.
segments.headline: The biggest canyon

segments.text: Valles Marineris is about four thousand kilometers long. On Earth, it would stretch across the entire United States.
Earth's Grand Canyon is about four hundred and fifty kilometers long. Mars beats it almost ten times over.
segments.headline: Grand Canyon? Tiny

segments.text: In places, it's seven kilometers deep, and two hundred kilometers wide.
It was discovered by Mariner nine, the first spacecraft to orbit another planet, in nineteen seventy-one. That's where its name comes from.
segments.headline: Named for Mariner 9

segments.text: But no river carved it. As the giant Tharsis volcanoes swelled up, the crust of Mars cracked and pulled apart.
segments.headline: The crust cracked

segments.text: Then giant landslides collapsed its walls, and water may have flowed through later.
segments.headline: Giant landslides

segments.text: Standing at the bottom, the far wall could be beyond the horizon. You might not even see it was a canyon.
segments.headline: Too big to see

segments.text: Tomorrow, we look up from the canyon at a small moon racing across the Martian sky. A moon that is slowly falling into Mars. Follow, so you don't miss episode ninety-eight.
